ai.title: Refactor agent loading and validation logic
ai.summary: Refactored `fetchAgentFromDatabase` in `backend/src/templates/agent-registry.ts` to validate agents using their original `agentId` before assigning the full `publisher/agentId@version` identifier to the final template. Updated `npm-app/src/index.ts` to conditionally load local agents only when no specific agent is requested, preventing unnecessary initialization. Adjusted `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts` to accommodate the new async structure for local agent assembly.

eli5.text: The tool now checks agents with their simpler original name before wrapping them in their full published name, so agent validation happens in the right order. When you run a specific agent on purpose, the tool no longer bothers loading the others sitting on your disk first. This is live today as behind-the-scenes maintenance. You won't see a new setting or menu item, but if you launch a named agent, things start up cleanly without the extra setup that used to happen regardless.

ai.title: Update open source agent models and types
ai.summary: Open source agent configurations updated: `researcher.ts` switches to `z-ai/glm-4.5:fast`, `thinker.ts` to `qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-thinking-2507:fast`. Type definitions in `agent-config.d.ts` and `tools.d.ts` refined for `ToolResult` and parameter formatting. `tool-renderers.ts` refactored to remove `AGENT_PERSONAS` dependency, using local `SpawnAgentConfig` interface.

eli5.text: The assistant can now choose from different AI brains for its specialist helpers, one for digging up research facts now uses z-ai/glm-4.5, and the deep-thinking helper now uses qwen/qwen3-235b, so each helper picks the best tool for its job instead of sharing one default. Behind the scenes, the instructions telling the helpers how to talk to each other were also cleaned up, which removes an old dependency that linked two parts of the system together. If you watched the helpers running, you wouldn't see anything different on screen today, since the switch just changes which AI model answers each question behind the curtain.

ai.title: codebuff 1.0.455
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.455 in npm-app/release/package.json. Minor internal release.

eli5.text: If you use the coding assistant on the web, the referral banner at the top of the screen will now stay hidden once your account is more than one week old. This release bundles several smaller fixes: the assistant loads its internal helpers more reliably, some open-source model settings were refreshed, the --agent flag now resolves helpers correctly, the referral banner hides for accounts older than a week, and the WebSocket connection layer was modernized. Installing or updating to this version is required for these changes to take effect; older versions keep the old behavior.

ai.title: Fix subagent resolution for --agent flag
ai.summary: Backend now skips dynamic subagent injection when `agentId` is provided, preventing `--agent` from modifying configured subagents. CLI unconditionally loads local agents to ensure config availability for this check. Updated `.agents/file-explorer.ts` to use local `file-picker` reference instead of versioned `codebuff/file-picker`.

eli5.text: When you tell the tool to use a specific assistant with the --agent option, that choice now properly sticks instead of being quietly overridden. Previously, the tool would still sneak in extra helper assistants even when you picked a specific one; now it respects your pick. Also, the built-in file-searching helper now reliably finds its matching picker tool instead of occasionally reaching for the wrong one, making it more stable when running behind the scenes.

ai.title: Hide referral banner for accounts older than one week
ai.summary: Referral banner now checks `userProfile.created_at` to hide itself for accounts older than 7 days. New `useUserProfile` hook fetches `/api/user/profile` with 5-minute `staleTime` and caches in localStorage under `codebuff-user-profile`. Banner component gates visibility on `isNewAccount` computed from the profile timestamp. Scope: `web/src/components/ui/banner.tsx`, `web/src/hooks/use-user-profile.ts`, `web/src/app/api/user/profile/route.ts`.

eli5.text: If you've had a CodeBuff account for more than a week, the referral banner that used to pop up at the top of the page will no longer appear for you, it only shows to accounts less than seven days old. To make that happen, the system now checks the date your account was created and hides the banner automatically once that week is up. You wouldn't notice this unless you're a very new user: new accounts still see the banner as before, while older accounts simply load without it, no action needed on your part.

ai.title: SDK 0.1.0 adds WebSocketHandler, drops CodebuffClient types
ai.summary: The SDK bumps to @codebuff/sdk 0.1.0 and introduces sdk/src/websocket-client.ts exporting WebSocketHandler and WebSocketHandlerOptions, while removing sdk/src/types.ts and its CodebuffClientOptions, ChatContext, NewChatOptions, and ContinueChatOptions exports that sdk/src/client.ts no longer imports. sdk/src/constants.ts adds IS_DEV, IS_TEST, IS_PROD, WEBSOCKET_URL, WEBSITE_URL, and BACKEND_URL constants that branch on the NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT variable to select prod or local WebSocket and site endpoints. common/src/actions.ts deletes ResponseCompleteSchema and the tool-call, terminal-command-result, npm-version-status, and commit-message-response server actions along with the FileVersionSchema import, and npm-app/src/client.ts removes the corresponding npm-version-status warning subscription and generateCommitMessage method.
ai.evidence: sdk/package.json bumps @codebuff/sdk from 0.0.3 to 0.1.0; sdk/src/websocket-client.ts is a new file exporting WebSocketHandler and WebSocketHandlerOptions; sdk/src/types.ts is deleted; sdk/src/constants.ts adds IS_DEV, IS_TEST, IS_PROD, WEBSOCKET_URL, WEBSITE_URL, and BACKEND_URL reading the NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT variable; common/src/actions.ts removes ResponseCompleteSchema plus the tool-call, terminal-command-result, npm-version-status, and commit-message-response server actions and the FileVersionSchema import; npm-app/src/client.ts drops the npm-version-status and commit-message-response subscriptions and generateCommitMessage; common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts changes onError to accept a WebSocket error event.
ai.migration: If you import CodebuffClientOptions, ChatContext, NewChatOptions, or ContinueChatOptions from the SDK, update your types to WebSocketHandlerOptions or inline object shapes, since sdk/src/types.ts was deleted.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show an index file re-exporting WebSocketHandler, so the public import path for consumers is not visible.

changes.what: Bumped @codebuff/sdk to 0.1.0, added sdk/src/websocket-client.ts exporting WebSocketHandler and WebSocketHandlerOptions, deleted sdk/src/types.ts, and inlined option types in sdk/src/client.ts.
Added IS_DEV, IS_TEST, IS_PROD, WEBSOCKET_URL, WEBSITE_URL, and BACKEND_URL constants in sdk/src/constants.ts driven by the NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT variable.

Removed ResponseCompleteSchema and the tool-call, terminal-command-result, npm-version-status, and commit-message-response server actions from common/src/actions.ts along with the FileVersionSchema import.
Dropped the npm-version-status and commit-message-response subscriptions and the generateCommitMessage method from npm-app/src/client.ts to match the removed server actions.
Changed APIRealtimeClient.onError in common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts to accept a WebSocket error event argument.

ai.title: Remove temp type from WebSocket client
ai.summary: Removed `asdf` type from `sdk/src/websocket-client.ts`. This was a temporary utility type excluding specific `ServerAction` types. No functional impact on WebSocket handling.

eli5.text: The WebSocket client no longer carries a temporary helper that listed which server message types it should ignore. Because that helper was never used to drive behavior, removing it changes nothing you would experience as a user; the connection continues to filter messages the same way. You would only notice if you happened to inspect the client code and found that short list of excluded types gone. This cleanup is live today as part of routine code maintenance.

ai.title: SDK sendInput replaces init action
ai.summary: WebSocketHandler gains sendInput and cancelInput methods, injecting apiKey into prompt and cancel-user-input actions. The legacy init action and its generate-commit-message schema variant are removed from common/src/actions.ts. This shifts authentication from explicit init calls to implicit injection via getInputDefaultOptions in sdk/src/websocket-client.ts.

eli5.text: The software development kit used to require a separate authentication step before it could talk to the service. That separate step is gone; the SDK now handles authentication automatically every time it sends input or cancels a request, using your API key in the background. Anyone building tools on top of the SDK no longer needs to call the old init function, and the new behavior was already merged and is available today.

ai.title: WebSocketHandler optional callbacks
ai.summary: SDK exports WebSocketHandler and getInitialSessionState from index.ts. WebSocketHandlerOptions callbacks onWebsocketError, onWebsocketReconnect, onRequestReconnect, onResponseError, onCostResponse, onUsageResponse, onResponseChunk, onSubagentResponseChunk, onPromptResponse are now optional. Internal fields use Required<WebSocketHandlerOptions> for type safety. Affects sdk/src/index.ts and sdk/src/websocket-client.ts.

eli5.text: When you connect the assistant to your own software using the provided toolkit, you no longer have to set up every optional callback handler up front. Functions that were previously required when wiring up a connection are now optional, so you can skip supplying handlers for things like connection retries, cost notifications, or response events unless you actually need them. For developers building on top of the toolkit, this means the initial setup is simpler and you only add the pieces you care about.

ai.title: Update SDK README to WebSocketHandler
ai.summary: SDK docs replaced `CodebuffClient` with `WebSocketHandler` and `getInitialSessionState`. Prerequisites now use `codebuff login` instead of `export CODEBUFF_API_KEY`. Full event callback and session state setup provided.

eli5.text: If you use the Codebuff software development kit, the setup instructions just got simpler: instead of manually pasting your API key into a terminal command, you now just run a single login command that saves your credentials for you. The example code in the readme also got a friendlier interface, with clearer names for the connection handler and more detailed callbacks showing when it connects, reconnects, or runs into problems. Who this affects: anyone following the SDK readme to connect their own tools to Codebuff. What you'd notice if you looked: the old 'CodebuffClient' class is gone, replaced by 'WebSocketHandler', and the example shows a much more complete picture of all the events you can react to.

ai.title: Add ai 4.3.16 to common and sdk
ai.summary: Added `ai` version `4.3.16` as a dependency to `common/package.json` and `sdk/package.json`. This introduces the Vercel AI SDK to the core packages, likely to support shared AI model interactions or streaming utilities. Scope covers the shared `common` and `sdk` packages.

eli5.text: The assistant software now has a shared toolbox for talking to AI models that both of its main parts can use. If you were building or extending the assistant, you would notice that the code for handling model interactions lives in one common place instead of being copied into each part. This is a behind-the-scenes change, so you as a user won't see a new button or different response style; it makes the system easier to maintain and helps keep AI features consistent across the assistant. It's already live in today's version.

ai.title: SDK version bump to 0.1.1
ai.summary: Bump @codebuff/sdk to 0.1.1 in sdk/package.json. Version metadata change only. No functional or API changes.

eli5.text: You, as a developer using the Codebuff SDK, got a new version of the development kit that you just installed. Nothing actually works differently when you update to this version. It is like getting a new box for your Lego set where all the pieces are exactly the same as before, just the box is slightly different. The change is only in the packaging information that tells your computer which version of the tool it is working with.

ai.title: Add agent store web page and API route
ai.summary: Added web/src/app/agents/page.tsx and web/src/app/api/agents/route.ts to expose a browsable agent store. The GET /api/agents route queries @codebuff/common/db for published agentConfig rows, joins publisher data, dedupes by name to keep latest versions, and returns mock usage metrics. web/src/components/navbar/navbar.tsx links to /agents via a new Agent Store entry. npm-app/src/cli-handlers/agents.ts drops unused startAgentCreationChat and createAgentFromRequirements imports.

eli5.text: If you visit the web app, you'll now see an Agent Store link in the main navigation menu. Clicking that link opens a new page where you can browse published agents in a searchable, sortable grid. Behind the scenes, a new API endpoint pulls agent data from the database and returns it with basic usage metrics, and the CLI tool sheds some unused code that no longer serves a purpose. The store is live and visible right now to anyone who opens the site.

ai.title: Comment out Agent Store links in navbar
ai.summary: Agent Store navigation links commented out in web/src/components/navbar/navbar.tsx. Removal targets both desktop and mobile dropdown views. Internal UI change; no user action required.

eli5.text: The website's main menu bar used to have a link that visitors could click (or tap, on a phone) to open a page showing a collection of pre-built assistants, labeled 'Agent Store.' That link has now been turned off in both the desktop and phone versions of the menu, so it is no longer visible to anyone who opens the site. People browsing the site will simply see a 'Pricing' option followed by any account-related choices, but the row of assistant listings that used to be selectable from the top menu is gone.
